      Problem: A new hard dependency on sha256sum is enforced at script startup via command -v sha256sum ... || exit 1. This binary is only needed for the cross-cycle escalation feature, but the check makes it mandatory for all validation runs.; On platforms without sha256sum (e.g., macOS runners with shasum instead), the script exits immediately rather than failing open gracefully. This is inconsistent with the pyflakes/ruff fail-open convention used elsewhere in the same file.; Issue 4: Tab-Stripping Logic in F-Code Lint Could Flatten Python Indentation

  [2] File: scripts/validate_process.sh
      Problem: The guard if FINGERPRINT_TITLES="$(jq -r '.fix_issues | sort_by(.title // "") | map(.title // "") | join("\n")' "${DIAGNOSE_RESULT_FILE}" 2>/dev/null)"; then is a shell anti-pattern. The exit status of an assignment statement is 0 unless the assignment itself fails. The exit status of the command substitution does not affect the condition. Therefore this branch always executes even when jq fails or returns empty, and FAILURE_FINGERPRINT would be computed from empty input (printf '' | sha256sum), yielding a deterministic non-empty hash.; Escalation to harness_error may fire incorrectly when jq fails (false positive), or conversely may not fire when the same fingerprint repeats but jq partial failures produce unexpected hashes (false negative). This undermines the reliability of the cross-cycle safety net.; Issue 3: sha256sum Hard Dependency Only Needed for Cross-Cycle Feature
      Confidence: avg 4.0
      Flagged by: deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5

  [3] File: scripts/validate_process.sh
      Problem: When strip_tabs is true (from <<- heredoc syntax), the code strips ALL leading tabs: body = '\n'.join(line.lstrip('\t') for line in body.splitlines()). In Python code, tabs are legitimate indentation tokens that define code blocks.; If a heredoc contains nested Python structures (if/for/def with tab indentation), stripping all leading tabs flattens nested structures and could cause IndentationError at runtime. While the script later runs ast.parse(body) to verify syntax, the flattened body might pass AST parsing if all indentation is uniformly removed but fail at actual execution when the runner executes the original script with real tabs.; Issue 5: pyflakes/ruff Tool Invocation Failure Treated as Lint Violations

      Problem: When handling `<<-` heredocs, the code strips all leading tabs from every line. While this serves to dedent the block relative to the shell script, it also flattens any legitimate nested indentation within the Python code itself (which often uses tabs in these generated scripts).; A nested Python block like `if True:\n\t\tprint("nested")` will be flattened to `if True:\nprint("nested")`, causing an `IndentationError` when passed to `ast.parse` or the linters, leading to false-positive preflight failures.; ### Issue 2: Tool runtime errors block preflight instead of failing open

  [17] File: `scripts/validate_process.sh` (line ~1312)
      Problem: If `pyflakes` or `ruff` encounter an environment error (e.g., `OSError`, `TimeoutExpired`), the `run_tool` function returns an error message which is then added to the `errors` list. Any item in the `errors` list causes the script to `sys.exit(1)`.; This violates the project's "fail-open" convention for optional linters. If a tool times out due to system load or fails due to a transient filesystem issue, the entire validation preflight fails, blocking the PR workflow. Tool execution failures should be warnings, not hard errors.; ### Issue 3: Ineffective `jq` exit status check in fingerprinting
